fatal_errors: The hypothesis attributes low strength to intrinsically high stacking-fault energy, but no cited evidence establishes high stacking-fault energy in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.

E1 concerns CrCoNi and reports very low or negative stacking-fault energy, while E2 and E3 concern a multiphase, precipitate-strengthened alloy; none supports the proposed single-phase CoCrFeNiTi mechanism.
The proposed strain-rate, temperature, and composition variations do not reconstruct the HEBM-plus-SPS intervention or its nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structural mediator.

The falsification rule does not directly test the central high-stacking-fault-energy claim; failure of altered loading or composition to generate twins or precipitates would not falsify high dislocation mobility in the starting alloy.
explanation: The response addresses deformation and low strength in the stated alloy and gives broad composition, phase-state, and loading boundaries. However, it misses the target controlled comparison based on milling duration and SPS temperature, including the specified 400 rpm, 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, 900–1000 °C sintering window, and 10-minute hold. It also omits the target mechanism—nanocrystalline Hall–Petch strengthening, milling-induced dislocation density, solid-solution strengthening, densification, and stabilization of an approximately 83% FCC/17% BCC structure—and provides no predictions corresponding to about 675 HV hardness or 1894 MPa compressive strength. Its alternative high-SFE mechanism is not validated by the supplied evidence. A discriminating test would directly measure stacking-fault energy or partial-dislocation separation while independently controlling grain size, phase fraction, density, and dislocation density; the proposed experiment instead changes several variables and uses a non-diagnostic falsification criterion.
